# Cadence Design Systems

## Strong Results/Guide on Record Backlog and Agentic AI Proof Points
Reinforcing Increased EDA Usage Thesis; Reit OW, PT Raised to $420

  
---  
  
By Harlan Sur
AC,
Akanksh
Chauhan,
Mayur
Ramdhani,
Apoorva
Kumar

Click here for the full document and
disclaimers

| Overweight  
---  
CDNS, CDNS US  
Price (26 Oct 26):$322.17  
**▲** Price Target (Dec-27):$420.00  
Prior (Dec-27):$405.00  
  
Cadence’s (CDNS) 3Q26 beat and raise on the FY26 guide point to continued
strong chip design activity and monetization of its AI agentic portfolio of
products. 3Q revenue (+22% y/y) and EPS both came in above the high end of
guidance, with backlog exiting the quarter at a record $8.2B (fifth
consecutive quarter of backlog growth). Growth was up double-digit % across
all product groups, with core EDA up 20% y/y, IP up 24%, SD&A up 30%, and
hardware product sales driving another record quarter. Growth drivers included
AI/HPC chip/ASIC design activity, advanced-node and chiplet/advanced packaging
adoption, and expanded commitments from several large semiconductor and
systems customers. At the midpoint, the updated FY26 outlook now implies ~21%
y/y revenue growth and ~$8.40 in EPS (vs. ~19% and ~$8.10 prior). YTD bookings
growth of 26% and recurring revenue trending 18% y/y (versus 10-11% last
year), suggest that AI/agent portfolio licensing add-on activity and deeper
customer engagements are driving growth. On the product side, the key
announcement from the print was Maestro, a family of AI models built
specifically for semiconductor and system design work that delivers up to 30%
higher quality and up to 5x greater token efficiency vs. general-purpose
closed foundation models. Customer traction is accelerating, as CDNS now has
100+ active engagements across all its AI agents, up from 45+ for ChipStack
and ViraStack combined last quarter. We believe these proof points support
management’s framing that agentic AI drives more, not less, usage of its core
EDA engines. CDNS also increased capital returns, doubling its quarterly
buyback to $400M and adding $2.5B to its repurchase authorization. While
Hexagon D&E will still be a drag on FY26 incremental margins, management
expects integration work to make it margin-accretive in 2027. Net-net, we
believe the clean beat-and-raise, record backlog, and evidence of agentic AI
moving into production should drive further upward estimate revisions and add
to confidence in CDNS’s medium-term growth outlook. As such, we reiterate our
OW rating and raise our CY26 and CY27 estimates and our Dec-27 PT to $420
(from $405), based on 43x our CY27 EPS estimate of $9.85, in line with
comparable tech/design software/IP peers.

  * 3Q26 results came in above the high end of guidance on broad-based, double-digit growth across all product groups, with backlog reaching a record high… CDNS exited 3Q with a record backlog of $8.2B (vs. $8.1B in 2Q) and reported 3Q revenues of $1.63B (+22% y/y, +3% q/q), above the high end of its $1.595-$1.625B guide and our $1.61B estimate. Strength was broad-based across all lines of business. Core EDA grew 20% y/y on 16 new digital full-flow wins and rising verification usage at hyperscaler and memory customers; hardware delivered another record quarter on sustained AI/HPC demand for Palladium and Protium; IP grew 24% y/y on custom silicon, advanced-node, and chiplet demand; and SD&A grew 30% y/y, supported by Millennium adoption and Allegro competitive displacement. EPS of $2.11 (+9% y/y) also came in above guidance and our $2.04 estimate. Operating margin of 44.1% also beat guidance and was roughly in line with our ~44.0% estimate, though down from 47.6% a year ago, partly reflecting the lower-margin Hexagon D&E contribution. 
  * 4Q guide well ahead of our prior estimates, and FY26 guidance is raised to 21% y/y growth… For 4Q26, CDNS guided revenue to $1.71B at the midpoint (+19% y/y, +5% q/q) and EPS to $2.22, both well above our prior estimates of $1.63B and $2.00. For FY26, the revenue guide moved up to a $6.40B midpoint (from $6.30B prior), which implies ~21% y/y growth. CDNS also raised its EPS guide to a midpoint of $8.40 (from $8.10 prior), and guided OPM to 44.7% at the midpoint, with operating cash flow unchanged at ~$2B. Although Hexagon D&E is contributing little operating profit this year, management noted that incremental operating margins excluding it remain within CDNS’s typical 54-55% range and expects progress on its integration to make it margin-accretive in 2027. On capital returns, CDNS expects to repurchase ~$400M of shares again in 4Q and to use >50% of FY26 free cash flow for buybacks. 
  * Raising CY26/CY27 estimates and increasing our PT to $420… Given the strong results and guidance, we are increasing our CY26 and CY27 estimates and raising our Dec-27 price target to $420. Our PT assumes CDNS trades at 40-45x (43x) our CY27 EPS estimate of ~$9.85, in line with comparable peers in the tech/design software IP space.

CLS, CLS US  
Price (26 Oct 26):$246.65  
  
Celestica’s 3Q26 results and updated 2027 outlook continue to point to a
robust demand environment and further room to expand operating margins, which
we expect to be well received by investors. That said, the lingering question
heading into the earnings call and analyst day is likely to be working capital
requirements and FCF into 2027 and beyond.

For 3Q26, revenue of $5.8 bn came in above JPMe, consensus, and the high end
of the guidance range, driven by particularly strong Compute & Storage demand.
Meanwhile, the 4Q26 guide was more mixed as revenue tracked below JPMe and was
largely in line with consensus, operating margins were modestly better than
both JPMe and consensus, and earnings came in softer than both heading into
the print. Separately, management lowered FCF guidance to $460 mn in 2026 (vs.
JPMe of $466 mn and prior guidance of $600mn), citing “targeted working
capital investments to support the accelerating growth in 2027.”

Looking ahead to 2027, revenue is guided to $40 bn, or +90% y/y, well ahead of
both JPMe and consensus as management reinforced the strength of demand by
noting that its 2028 forecast is “meaningfully higher” than the 2027 outlook.
Operating margin guidance for 2027 also came in ahead of JPMe and consensus,
together supporting solid EPS upside relative to consensus. Notably, the press
release did not include FCF guidance for 2027, following a reduction to FCF
guidance for 2026, which is likely to be an area of focus heading into the
earnings call and analyst day.

Celestica is hosting an earnings call tomorrow at 8:00 AM ET, which can be
accessed via
webcast.

Meta Platforms Inc  
---  
Anticipation becomes a reality, Meta announces equity
raise  
---  
| | Reiterate Rating: BUY  
---  
PO:845.00 USD   |   Price:638.06 USD  
| Equity   |   26 October 2026  
---  
---  
---  
---  
Key takeaways  
---  
  
  * Meta plans to raise approx. $35bn through Class A stock and convertible preferred, plus up to $60bn through a Class C ATM.
  * The magnitude of financing suggests upside risk Street capex estimates; we also est. up to 6% dilutive to EPS.
  * We think a raise was expected, and stock performance from here will depend on traction for AI initiatives; Maintain Buy.

  
---  
| FULL REPORT|     |   
---|---|---  
  
* * *  
  
---  
  
Meta plans to raise up to $100bn in capital

Meta announced plans that could raise up to $95-$100bn, including $22.5bn
Class A common stock, ~$12.5bn mandatory convertible preferred and an up to
$60bn Class C ATM program expected to begin no earlier than 1Q'27\. The Class
A and preferred offerings also include 15% greenshoe options, potentially
increasing the initial raise by $5bn. Bloomberg reported the preferred could
carry a 6.5% dividend and 17.5%-22.5% conversion premium. Meta also noted that
NVIDIA, AMD and Broadcom have indicated interest in purchasing up to $5bn of
Class A offering. Meta intends to use the proceeds for general corporate
purposes, including continued investment in AI infrastructure. Our Take: For
use of equity vs debt, our high-level analysis suggests that a ~$100bn debt
raise at 7% interest could be 6.8% dilutive to 2027 EPS, while raising similar
amount in equity at average price of ~$640, or ~157mn shares, would only be
6.5% dilutive. Assuming $95bn is raised at a stock price at around $640 (and
including the convertible stock as equity), we estimate Meta would issue
roughly 150mn shares, which would be ~6% dilutive to EPS, or up to ~$2
negative impact to our 2027 EPS estimates of $34.00.

Financing signals ongoing infrastructure investment cycle

In the press release, Meta highlighted that it is building four 1GW+
superclusters and expects to nearly double infrastructure capacity y/y in 2026
(we estimated that Meta started the year with 3-3.5GW). The company also
reiterated its growing AI opportunities across consumer and enterprise, with
early product adoption and multiple emerging monetization opportunities
supporting demand for incremental compute capacity. Our Take: We estimate
$210bn in capex and $32bn in negative FCF in 2027 (we think some on buyside
are around $240bn in capex, and others are even higher). The financing
potentially being raised at $95bn suggests higher capex than BofA/Street
estimates in 2027.

Higher capital intensity increases focus on returns

An equity raise was expected, in our view, and announcement clears up some
uncertainty on magnitude and timing. Key investor concerns are likely to
include: 1) higher and potentially more persistent capex, with the financing
raising questions around the magnitude of investment beyond 2027 (Street
currently estimates 2027/2028 capex of ~$216bn/$235bn), 2) dilution overhang
from the planned up to $60bn Class C ATM program, and 3) the risk that AI
infrastructure investment scales faster than monetization, pressuring FCF and
margins near term. We think the key debate will increasingly center on whether
incremental AI monetization can scale fast enough to support a structurally
higher investment base, with Muse adoption, Business Agent monetization and
enterprise AI likely key proof points. We also think Meta will continue to
push the ad business to support the stock price. Given a big AI opportunity
ahead, we maintain our Buy rating.

| | | ORCL will host its Investor Day this Wednesday, October 28, at AI World in Las Vegas. We preview our expectations and key items to watch from the credit lens.   
---  
| | Key takeaways  
---  
  
  * Historical rally-then-reverse patterns suggest potential near-term relief with event, though same-day FOMC and hyperscaler earnings may complicate reaction. 
  * We maintain a medium-term cautious view; ORCL's credit story is not just about securing financing, but also leverage, contract mismatch, execution, counterparty risks. 
  * We expect IG and ~$40bn FY27 funding reiterations, alongside limited LT clarity & a list of financing options to try to appeal to both debt & equity investors. 
  * We look for updates on RPO growth and quality, ambitious FY30 targets, and the timing of a consolidated FCF inflection. 
  * Key buildout watch items include contract economics, prepayments and financing support, new leases, and delivery delay risks.
